summary: A sound, narrow stage-3 step: a BLOCK_T 256 tile at T > 4096 halves the redundant per-token-tile dequant and doubles wgmma N per dequantized LHS, the turn shapes stay byte-identical, and the profile row for _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel at first_turn gives a clean milestone reading against stage 2's 9.1-10.0 ms. One concrete bug must be fixed while building: _check_expert_gemms as written breaks at BLOCK_T 256 (CHECK_ROWS 128 < 256), so prepare() would assert and the whole run would fail.
justification: Mechanism. With BLOCK_W 128 and num_warps 8, Triton's warpsPerTileV3 gives warpsPerCTA [8,1]. Each warpgroup then owns 64 W rows x all 256 tokens (wgmma m64n256k16, 128 fp32 acc regs/thread), as the hypothesis says. The register-A dequantized LHS is unchanged, so per K step the dequant ALU stays fixed while MMA work per program doubles. At ~512 local rows per expert (16384 local routes over 32 experts), token tiles per (expert, W tile) go from ~4.5 to ~2.5. Under the serialized model (ALU ~= MMA ~0.6 us/SM per 128x128x128), cost per (expert, W tile, K step) goes from ~4.5 x 1.2 to ~2.5 x 1.8 units, about 15-25% off after the extra padding. The <= 7.5 ms milestone is plausible but optimistic. Grid parallelism is fine: ~80 local token tiles x 64 (w13, N 8192) or 32 (w2, N 4096) W tiles is still tens of waves on 132 SMs. Smem: Triton multi-buffers every loop load, i.e. a_lo + a_hi (64 KB) + codes [128,64] u8 (8 KB) + scales (1 KB), about 73 KB per stage. Two stages is ~146 KB plus the epilogue's convert scratch, which fits the 227 KB limit. Three stages (~219 KB plus scratch) likely would not, so num_stages 2 is the right call. Shapes and directions agree with TASK: only T=16384 (> 4096) changes. turn_4 (T=3012) and the T=4096 test stay on the stage-2 BLOCK_T 128 config, and turn_1 on BLOCK_T 64. The headline arithmetic is overstated, though. The score is a geomean over three loads, and first_turn's load is ~3.14 s (16x16.5 + 138x15.9 + 16x19.6 + 16x23.2 ms), so 2 ms off each first_turn shape is ~12% on that load and ~+4% headline, not +6-8%. Weakest link: the premise that stage 2 is dequant-ALU-bound and serialized with the register-A wgmma is a reviewer estimate, not a measurement. If stage 2 is instead bound by the gathered activation loads' latency (row-gathered, no TMA, now only 2 stages deep), by register pressure, or by tail/imbalance (the identical expert math costs 9.15-10.0 ms across the four first_turn shapes, a 9% spread that larger tiles can amplify), BLOCK_T 256 can come out flat or slower. Register pressure is the most likely failure. Counting 128 acc + ~32 LHS + ~32 code + ~32 broadcast-scale regs plus addressing gives ~230-250 of the 255 allowed at 256 threads, so spills are a real possibility. The stated fallback (BLOCK_W 64 x BLOCK_T 256 at 4 warps) is the right next stage if so.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: no confounding. It fixes the modules around the experts (pooler/pre-expert norm feeding x, silu_and_mul, post-expert weighted sum), and this change touches only the expert GEMM tile config at T > 4096 on top of stage 2, which already carries parity. The comparison is the replaced kernel's own time per first_turn shape against stage 2 (00148fbedfb6414f) and Marlin, which parity does not affect.
interference: No companion is warranted. This is a rewrite stage judged on _moe_nvfp4_gemm_kernel's own us at the four first_turn shapes against stage 2's 10009/9909/9747/9146 us and Marlin's 10.2-12.0 ms. Triton kernel times reproduce within ~1% (LESSONS), so a single run reads cleanly. The run also carries a built-in drift control: the turn_1/turn_4 kernel rows run byte-identical stage-2 code (796/823 and 2158/2100 us). If they move by x%, discount the first_turn delta by that much. Compare first_turn row for row (same shape key), not as an average, because the kernel's time already varies 9% across those shapes. The only possible control, BLOCK_T 256 at num_stages 3 or GROUP_SIZE_T 8, would not disambiguate anything worth a check with prefill at 2 checks left. That and the BLOCK_W 64 fallback are next-stage material.
rules_flags: None against the rules: NVFP4 bank unchanged, dequant stays in registers, no BF16 weight copy, config picked from T (shape) only, no host sync, no autotune, nothing derived from inputs cached.

Correctness gate (not a rule, but it would fail the run): in _check_expert_gemms, CHECK_ROWS = 128 < BLOCK_T 256 gives CHECK_ROWS // bt == 0, so expert_ids[0] = -1 marks the one-hot block itself as non-local. w13 then never writes rows 0..127 (left NaN), the dequant assert fires and prepare() fails. Also total // bt = 2 entries for a grid of cdiv(640, 256) = 3 programs. Fix: per cfg, use check_rows = max(CHECK_ROWS, bt) rows (one-hot at k0 + r % 128 for every row, want rows tiled the same way), total = check_rows + 2*bt, expert_ids sized cdiv(total, bt), the -1 block at index check_rows // bt, the past-n_padded block at check_rows // bt + 1, and n_padded = check_rows + bt.

None of the 5 pre-timing tests has T > 4096, so the BLOCK_T 256 path meets real routing only in the timed first_turn calls (each still checked against the reference). The fixed prepare() check is its only correctness gate before timing, so make it cover the -1 block and the past-n_padded block at bt 256 exactly as for the other configs.
open_questions: Does Triton actually issue wgmma m64n256 with warpsPerCTA [8,1] here, and does the kernel spill? Record n_regs / n_spills from the compiled kernel's metadata in prepare() and print them, since the 16 KB log tail comes back with the run.

Is the register-A wgmma async across the next K step's dequant in the TTGIR (warp_group_dot with isAsync and a wait of 1 rather than 0)? If it waits on 0, the serialization premise holds and warp specialization or ping-pong is the real next lever, not more tile-size tuning.

Why does identical expert math take 9.15 ms at ctx 65536 but 10.0 ms at ctx 0? If it is routing skew per shape, larger token tiles raise tail cost on hot experts. Compare the stage-3 delta per shape to see whether the gain shrinks where stage 2 was slowest.
Correct the headline expectation to ~+4% (geomean over three loads) so a milestone-2 result is not read as a disappointment.
